subject: Physics
questionText: A block of mass 5 kg is pulled up a frictionless inclined plane of length 10 m and height 3 m by a force of 20 N parallel to the incline. If the block starts from rest, what is its velocity at the top of the incline?

optionsList.optionText: 4 m/s
6 m/s
8 m/s
10 m/s

solutionSteps.stepText: Calculate the work done on the block by the force as it moves up the incline.

optionsList.optionText: Work = Force * distance = 20 N * 10 m = 200 J
Work = Force * height = 20 N * 3 m = 60 J
Work = Force / distance = 20 N / 10 m = 2 J
Work = Force - distance = 20 N - 10 m = 10 J

solutionSteps.stepText: Apply the Work-Energy Theorem to find the final kinetic energy of the block.

optionsList.optionText: ΔKE = W = 200 J

solutionSteps.stepText: Use the kinetic energy equation to solve for the final velocity of the block.

optionsList.optionText: KE = 0.5 * m * v^2 => v = sqrt(2*KE/m) = sqrt(2*200/5) = sqrt(80) = 8.94 m/s, round to 9 m/s
KE = 0.5 * m * v^2 => v = sqrt(2*200/5) = sqrt(80) = 8.94 m/s, round to 6 m/s
KE = 0.5 * m * v^2 => v = sqrt(2*200/5) = sqrt(80) = 8.94 m/s, round to 10 m/s

15 m/s
20 m/s

solutionSteps.stepText: Apply the Work-Energy Theorem to find the final kinetic energy of the block.

optionsList.optionText: ΔKE = W = 50 J

solutionSteps.stepText: Use the kinetic energy equation to solve for the final velocity of the block.

solutionSteps.stepText: Calculate the work done by the force on the block.

solutionSteps.stepText: Calculate the work done against gravity.
